body.statement: Djuazon and Tsyawo's Theorem 1, specialized to the standard-normal working distribution, threshold \(y_0=0\), and the fixed pairs \(\mathcal P\), identifies \(\Delta_{\ell}=H(r_{\ell1},r_{\ell2},r_{\ell3})-r_{\ell4}\) for every \(\ell\), and hence identifies \(\overline\Delta=L^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{L}\Delta_{\ell}\). Outcome-independent splitting changes only the samples used to estimate the four observed marginals and does not alter this population identity.
body.justification: This published baseline fixes the causal estimand and prevents the rare-boundary analysis from being mistaken for a new identification claim.
body.gap: There is no novelty claim: this is exactly the standard-normal, threshold-zero specialization of Djuazon and Tsyawo's published identification formula.
body.consumer: Every boundary approximation and confidence set inherits the causal probability interpretation of the published DTT functional.
